size.note: Newman's Birds gives 135 cm on the Pink-backed Pelican page.

habitat: The colour key says inland waters.
summary: The colour key says the non-breeding bird has grey wings and is paler when breeding. The description paragraph on this page is the Great White Pelican account, also printed on the Great White Pelican page, so it was not used. Status and months are unset. The voice is not in the colour key. The Kemp paper name Pinkbacked Pelican and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Great White Pelican is the larger all-white bird. The Pink-backed colour key gives grey wings when not breeding.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 4–16.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: Paler than the non-breeding bird. No separate breeding colours were named in the colour key.

calls.description: The colour key does not describe the voice. The description paragraph is the Great White Pelican account and was not used. Grade B call from near Kassel, Ziguinchor, Senegal. No grade A recording was in the catalogue. The filename is XC862719-Pelican-gris-231215-0700-1CB-Senegal-Kasel-MixPre32-225.mp3.
